thread_text:
incident-bot: Alert: Persistent KV paging observed on cont-batch pool-apac-2; multiple customers affected. Severity: P1. Link: https://redwood/incident/2350001111

incident-bot: Symptoms: p99 latency spikes, backend 5xx rate increase, kvcache_pgfaults/sec elevated, swap usage climbing.

oncall-lee: I'm taking this pager. Quick snapshot?

sre-ash: pool-apac-2. kvcache.size went from 512MB -> 9.3GB over 11m. disk_iowait up, p99 generation > 10s. Recent profile push at 02:20 set max_batch_tokens=24576 and max_num_seqs=400 to optimize throughput.

runtime-tori: That profile also toggled batch_token_behavior=aggressive and enabled seq_packing=true. We've seen these knobs produce oversized logical batches when traffic has many short seqs.

platform-rahul: Rolling temporary traffic diversion: shifting 50% to pool-apac-1 and 25% to pool-us-east as relief. Will open canary for a config patch on the remaining 25%.

deploy-bot: Traffic split applied. Routes updated.

customer-success-ana: Two customers reported: analytics-runner (heavy multi-query) and inbox-proxy (chat). Analytics-runner has many multipart requests; inbox-proxy sees timeouts and user-facing errors. Both reported SLA violations.

sre-ash: Immediate mitigation option A: hard-cap max_batch_tokens to 8192 and set max_num_seqs=96. Option B: enable reject_on_paging=true at ingress so new batch requests that would cause paging are rejected with 429. Prefer A + short-term B if paging persists.

oncall-lee: I prefer A first to avoid mass rejections. Platform, can you apply A as a canary on 25%? Also prepare B as a hotflip if canary doesn't stabilize.

platform-rahul: Applying canary patch: 
```
kubectl -n inference patch cont-batch-profile apac-2 --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/max_batch_tokens","value":8192},{"op":"replace","path":"/max_num_seqs","value":96},{"op":"replace","path":"/batch_token_behavior","value":"conservative"}]'
```
Canary applied to 25% nodes.

deploy-bot: Canary started. 3/3 canary instances passing health checks.

runtime-tori: Observing canary nodes: kvcache.growth_rate dropping, page_faults down 60%, p99 latency on canary path improved. Small increase in per-token cpu but acceptable.

infra-bot: Disk swap pressure reduced on canary hosts; eviction events increased as expected.

customer-success-ana: Customer note: analytics-runner errors reduced by 80% on canary routing. inbox-proxy improved but still seeing some tail errors on non-canary path.

sre-ash: Proceed with progressive rollout to 75% over 8 minutes. Keep reject_on_paging ready.

platform-rahul: Rolling to 75% now. deploy-bot: Rollout 75% complete.

runtime-tori: Post-rollout metrics: cluster-wide kvcache stabilized at ~1.1GB growth over baseline, page faults dropped 78%, 5xx rate back to baseline. Token throughput reduced ~18% globally.

oncall-lee: Customer impact timeline: 02:20 - 02:40 UTC: elevated 5xxs and timeouts affecting 4 customers; mitigations restored baseline by 02:48. Duration ~28 minutes for majority recovery.

sre-ash: Root cause: an over-aggressive cont-batch profile (big max_batch_tokens and high max_num_seqs) combined with seq_packing and batch_token_behavior=aggressive caused KV index blowout and paging. Missing alert for rapid kvcache growth and missing ingress guard for oversized logical batches.

platform-rahul: Action items: 1) add an ingress guard rejecting batches > 12k tokens or > 160 seqs, 2) add kvcache_growth_rate alert (>=50%/5m), 3) revert profile defaults to conservative presets, 4) add pre-deploy simulation for cont-batch profile changes.

oncall-lee: I'll file the postmortem and notify account teams. Also adding follow-up ticket to evaluate reject_on_paging UX and potential client-side retry guidance.

incident-bot: Incident downgraded to P2 at 2350001190 by oncall-lee
